title: Lions Survive 21-Point Collapse, Beat Saints 31-30 in Overtime on Failed Two-Point Conversion
dek: The Detroit Lions defeated the New Orleans Saints 31-30 in overtime in Week 1 after blowing a 21-point lead, stopping Tyler Shough's two-point conversion pass incomplete on the final play with 1:34 remaining. The Saints nearly completed one of the NFL's historic comeback bids before the Lions' defensive stand ended the threat.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Lions held on to beat Saints 31-30 in overtime after Saints failed a two-point conversion attempt with 1:34 left in the extra period, forcing the defensive stop after blowing a 21-0 lead.
bottom_line: The Lions' second-half collapse raised immediate questions about defensive consistency. A single-point overtime victory against a Saints team that nearly erased a 21-point deficit leaves little margin for error in Detroit's Week 2 matchup.
body:
The Detroit Lions defeated the New Orleans Saints 31-30 in overtime in Week 1, holding on after the Saints clawed back from a 21-0 deficit in the second half. The Lions led 21-0 with less than nine minutes to play in the third quarter, per Yahoo NFL, only to see that advantage evaporate.
The Saints' comeback hinged on Tyler Shough's performance. The quarterback threw three interceptions and one fumble early in the game, per Yahoo NFL, then recovered to accumulate 411 passing yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions by game's end. Chris Olave finished with 10 catches for 182 yards in the loss, per Yahoo NFL. Noah Fant scored a touchdown that narrowed Detroit's lead to one point, per Yahoo NFL.
Shough connected with Juwan Johnson for a touchdown late in regulation to tie the game at 27-27, per Yahoo NFL. Daniel Carlson's 62-yard field goal attempt as time expired sailed wide, per Yahoo NFL, forcing both teams into overtime.
In the extra period, Amon-Ra St. Brown scored a touchdown to put the Lions back on track, according to Yahoo NFL.
Saints coach Kellen Moore opted to go for two on the overtime touchdown rather than playing for a likely tie, per Yahoo NFL. Shough's two-point pass fell incomplete on the final play with 1:34 left to play in overtime, per Yahoo NFL, ending New Orleans' bid.
